1.note: Here and throughout the chapter, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

2.note: By **send from the camp**, Yahweh means that the Israelites were to make certain people leave the camp and live outside it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall banish to a place outside the camp]

By **everyone flowing**, Moses means everyone who has an abnormal discharge from their genitals. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [everyone with abnormal discharge from their genitals]

Yahweh is using **unclean to a person** as a common expression of his culture to mean “unclean because of contact with a dead body.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unclean because of coming into contact with a corpse]

3.note: Yahweh is using the expression **From male up to female** as a common expression of his culture to mean “both males and females” or “everyone.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Both males and females]

It might seem that the expression **you shall send, to the outside of the camp you shall send them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [you shall send them to the outside of the camp]

The pronoun **you** here is in the plural form since Yahweh was speaking to Moses but wanted him to convey this command to all the Israelites. You could make this explicit if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [all of you must send] or [you Israelites must send]

3.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א יְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת־מַ֣חֲנֵי⁠הֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֥ן בְּ⁠תוֹכָֽ⁠ם
3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase (**where I am dwelling in the midst of them**) gives the reason for the result that the first phrase (**they shall not make unclean their camp**) describes. Alternate translation: [I am dwelling in the midst of them, so they shall not make unclean their camp]

The pronoun **they** refers to the unclean people who were sent outside the camp. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the unclean people shall not make unclean their camp]

4.q: וַ⁠יַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַ⁠יְשַׁלְּח֣וּ אוֹתָ֔⁠ם אֶל־מִ⁠ח֖וּץ לַֽ⁠מַּחֲנֶ֑ה
4.note: It might seem that the expression **the sons of Israel did so, and they sent them to the outside of the camp** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [And the sons of Israel sent them to the outside of the camp]

6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to the sons of Israel. Say to them that a man]

6.q: אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַעֲשׂוּ֙ מִ⁠כָּל־חַטֹּ֣את הָֽ⁠אָדָ֔ם לִ⁠מְעֹ֥ל מַ֖עַל בַּ⁠יהוָ֑ה וְ⁠אָֽשְׁמָ֖ה הַ⁠נֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַ⁠הִֽוא
6.note: In this verse, Yahweh alternates between singular and plural forms. He does this because the instructions relate to any person. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use just the singular or plural throughout this verse. Alternate translation: [A man or woman, when he or she does from all the sins of the man to be unfaithful {in} unfaithfulness against Yahweh, then that person is guilty] or [Men or women, when they do from all the sins of the man to be unfaithful {in} unfaithfulness against Yahweh, then those people are guilty]

Here, Yahweh could be using the possessive form to refer to **sins** that are: (1) committed against a **man**. Alternate translation: [the sins against a man] (2) committed by a **man**. Alternate translation: [the sins by a man]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [the human]

The words translated as **to be unfaithful** indicate that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [with the result that they are unfaithful]

Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to be very unfaithful]

The phrase **unfaithfulness** expresses an abstract idea. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **unfaithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in an unfaithful way]

7.q: וְ⁠הִתְוַדּ֗וּ אֶֽת־חַטָּאתָ⁠ם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂוּ֒ וְ⁠הֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־אֲשָׁמ⁠וֹ֙ בְּ⁠רֹאשׁ֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠חֲמִישִׁת֖⁠וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑י⁠ו וְ⁠נָתַ֕ן לַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם לֽ⁠וֹ
7.note: As in the previous verse, Yahweh alternates between singular and plural forms. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use just the singular or plural throughout this verse. Do what you did in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [And he or she shall confess his or her sin that he or she did, and he or she shall return his or her guilt in its head and he or she shall add its fifth upon it, and he or she shall give to him to whom he or she is guilty] or [And they shall confess their sin that they did, and they shall return their guilt in its head and they shall add its fifth upon it, and they shall give to him to whom they are guilty]

7.q: וְ⁠הֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־אֲשָׁמ⁠וֹ֙ בְּ⁠רֹאשׁ֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠חֲמִישִׁת֖⁠וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑י⁠ו וְ⁠נָתַ֕ן לַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָשַׁ֥ם לֽ⁠וֹ
7.note: Here the masculine pronouns **he**, **his**, and **him** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. This can be seen from verse 6, which explicitly refers to “a man or a woman.” If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and that person shall return his or her guilt in its head and he or she shall add its fifth upon it, and he or she shall give to the person to whom he or she is guilty]

Here, **guilt** represents the payment that must be made as compensation for causing damage or loss to someone. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the payment for his guilt]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **guilt**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his guilty payment]

Yahweh is using **in its head** as a common expression of his culture to mean “in its entirety” or “in full.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in its entirety]

Yahweh is using **add its fifth** as a common expression of his culture to mean “include an additional 20 percent.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall include a fifth more]
A **fifth** means one part out of five equal parts. Alternate translation: [and he shall add 20 percent]

Yahweh here refers to whomever the person sinned against. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [whom he sinned against when he became guilty]

8.note: The implication is that the wronged person has died and there are no close relatives who can receive the payment. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And if the person who was sinned against has died and there is not one redeeming for him]

The implication is that a **one redeeming** refers to a close relative who could receive payment on behalf of a deceased person who had been wronged. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a close relative who can represent the man]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [for the person to return the guilt to him or her]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **guilt**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the guilty payment to him, the guilty payment]

The term **guilt** represents “payment for guilt” or “compensation.” See how you translated the similar use of **guilt** in 5:7. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the payment for his guilt to him, the payment for the guilt]

The expression **being returned** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the guilt that the guilty person is returning]

The implication is that the payment belongs to Yahweh and therefore must be given to the priest who serves him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [is for Yahweh and thus given to the priest]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the ram for atoning upon which he shall atone for him]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **ram** that is used for **atonement**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the ram that is offered to atone]

The pronoun **he** refers to the priest, while the pronoun **him** refers to the guilty person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the priest shall make atonement for the guilty person]

Here the masculine term **him** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [for him or her]

9.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form **of the sons of Israel** to describe the **holy things** that are characterized by belonging to or coming from Israel. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And every holy contribution by the sons of Israel]

10.q: וְ⁠אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־קֳדָשָׁ֖י⁠ו ל֣⁠וֹ יִהְי֑וּ אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִתֵּ֥ן לַ⁠כֹּהֵ֖ן ל֥⁠וֹ יִהְיֶֽה
10.note: These two phrases **his holy things shall be to him** and **what he gives to the priest, to him shall be** mean basically the same thing, as long as **him** refers in both places to the priest (see the note below on these pronouns). The second phrase emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And a man, the holy things he gives to the priest shall be to him]

The phrase **a man … a man** is a common expression of his culture used to emphasize that this rule applies separately to each individual person. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [As for each man … as for each man]

The second occurrence of **him** refers to the priest. The first occurrence of **him** could refer to: (1) the priest. Alternate translation: [shall be to the priest … to the priest shall be] (2) the man who owns it before giving it to the priest. Alternate translation: [shall be to that man himself …to the priest shall be]

12.q: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם אִ֥ישׁ
12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak to the sons of Israel. Say to them that a man]

The phrase **and say to them** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.
In Hebrew, the repetition of **a man, a man** creates emphasis. If your language has different ways to show emphasis, you could use one of those instead. Alternate translation: [Any man]

These two phrases **turns aside** and **is unfaithful against him in unfaithfulness** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [his wife is unfaithful against him in unfaithfulness] or [his wife turns aside to unfaithfulness against him]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of a wife’s unfaithfulness as if she had literally **turned aside** from a path. This metaphor means that she has stopped being faithful to her husband. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his wife does what is wrong]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and is unfaithful against him]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **unfaithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in an unfaithful way]

13.note: Yahweh is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **lies with her the lying of seed**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [has sexual relations with her] or [commits adultery with her]

By **a man** Yahweh means a man who is not the woman’s husband. This would have been clear to the original readers from the context. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a man who is not her husband]

The expression **it is concealed from the eyes of her husband** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the eyes of her husband do not see it]

These two phrases **it is concealed from the eyes of her husband** and **it is hidden** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband]

Here, **from the eyes of her husband** represents her husband’s knowledge or awareness. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from her husband]

The expression **it is hidden** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and she hides it]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **she** separately, even though the verbs translated as **she is made unclean** and **she has … been caught** already include this meaning. He is doing that to switch from speaking about the husband to speaking about the wife. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that emphasis. Alternate translation: [and as for her, she is made unclean … and as for her, she has not been caught]

The expression **is made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and she, she has made herself unclean]

The expression **has not been caught** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one has caught her]

14.q: וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה וְ⁠קִנֵּ֥א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖⁠וֹ וְ⁠הִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙ וְ⁠קִנֵּ֣א & וְ⁠הִ֖יא לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה
14.note: It might seem that the second occurrence of the expression **a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him and he is jealous of his wife and she, she is made unclean or she, she is not made unclean]

14.q: וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה וְ⁠קִנֵּ֥א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖⁠וֹ & אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙ וְ⁠קִנֵּ֣א & וְ⁠הִ֖יא
14.note: The two phrases **a spirit of jealousy passes over on him** and **he is jealous** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could connect the phrases with a word other than **and** in order to show that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [and a spirit of jealousy passes over on him so that he is jealous of his wife … or a spirit of jealousy passes over on him so that he is jealous of his wife]

14.q: וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה & אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤י⁠ו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙
14.note: Yahweh is using **a spirit of jealousy passes over on him** as a common expression of his culture to mean “he feels jealous.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he feels jealous … or he feels jealous]

The expression **is made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and she, she has made herself unclean … and she, she has not made herself unclean]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **she** separately, even though the verbs translated as **she is made unclean** and **she is … made unclean** already include this meaning. He is doing that to switch from speaking about the husband to speaking about the wife. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that emphasis. Alternate translation: [and as for her, she is made unclean … and as for her, she is not made caught]

15.note: Yahweh is using **bring her offering upon her** as a common expression of his culture to mean “bring the offering for her.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he shall bring the offering for her]

This **ephah** was equivalent to 22 liters or nearly two thirds of a bushel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [about 2.2 liters] or [about two thirds of a bushel]
A **tenth** means one part out of ten equal parts. Alternate translation: [one-tenth]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **flour** that is made from **barley**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [flour made with barley]

15.q: לֹֽא־יִצֹ֨ק עָלָ֜י⁠ו שֶׁ֗מֶן וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִתֵּ֤ן עָלָי⁠ו֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה כִּֽי־מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ ה֔וּא מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the first phrase. The phrase **it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial causing iniquity to be remembered** gives the reason why **he shall not pour oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it**. Alternate translation: [It is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of memorial causing iniquity to be remembered, so he shall not pour oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it]

15.q: מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ & מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן
15.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **jealousy**, **memorial**, and **iniquity**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [a grain offering of a jealous husband, a grain offering that reminds a person and that causes any bad thing the person did to be remembered]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **grain offering** that is characterized by **jealousy** and serves as a **memorial**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a grain offering offered because of jealousy and to make a memorial]

The expression **to be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [causing people to remember iniquity]

16.note: The implication is that the priest presents the woman at the altar to have her stand before Yahweh for judgment. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall have her come near the altar]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

17.note: The implication is that the priest must first get water that was set apart for sacred use and then put it in a clay pot. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall fill a vessel of clay with holy water]

Yahweh is using **take from the dust** as a common expression of his culture to mean “take some of the dust.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the priest shall take some of the dust]

Here, Yahweh could mean that the priest should: (1) mix the dust in with the water. Alternate translation: [and he shall mix it into the water] (2) pour the dust on top of the water. Alternate translation: [and he shall pour it onto the water]

18.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

Here, the word **head** could refer to: (1) the woman’s hair. In this case, the priest lets down her hair. Alternate translation: [and he shall let the woman’s hair down] (2) the woman’s head, which has hair on it. In this case, the priest uncovers the woman’s head and her hair. Alternate translation: [and he shall uncover the head of the woman]

Yahweh is using **put on her palm** as a common expression of his culture to mean “hand to her” or “give to her to hold.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall hand her]

18.q: אֵ֚ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַ⁠זִּכָּר֔וֹן מִנְחַ֥ת קְנָאֹ֖ת הִ֑וא
18.note: See how you translated the phrases **grain offering of memorial** and **grain offering of jealousy** in 5:15.

Here, Yahweh could be using the possessive form to indicate that the **water**: (1) causes **bitterness** in the woman’s life. Alternate translation: [the water that causes a bitter life] (2) tastes bitter. Alternate translation: [the water that tastes bitter]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **bitterness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the water that makes bitter]

Here, **the water** represents the vessel containing the water that has been prepared with dust from the tabernacle floor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the vessel full of the water]

19.q: וְ⁠אָמַ֤ר אֶל־הָֽ⁠אִשָּׁה֙ אִם־לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔⁠ךְ וְ⁠אִם־לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑⁠ךְ הִנָּקִ֕י מִ⁠מֵּ֛י הַ⁠מָּרִ֥ים הַֽ⁠מְאָרֲרִ֖ים הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה׃ וְ⁠אַ֗תְּ כִּ֥י שָׂטִ֛ית תַּ֥חַת אִישֵׁ֖⁠ךְ וְ⁠כִ֣י נִטְמֵ֑את וַ⁠יִּתֵּ֨ן אִ֥ישׁ בָּ⁠ךְ֙ אֶת־שְׁכָבְתּ֔⁠וֹ מִֽ⁠בַּלְעֲדֵ֖י אִישֵֽׁ⁠ךְ
19.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and he shall tell the woman that if a man did not lie with her, and if she did not turn aside to uncleanness under her husband, she shall be free from the water of bitterness that brings a curse. And he will also tell that if she did turn aside under her husband, and if she was made unclean and a man gave his lying in her besides her husband,]

The priest is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **lie with you**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [a man did not have sexual relations with you] or [a man did not have intimate relations with you]

By **a man**, Yahweh means a man who is not the woman’s husband. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a man who is not your husband]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of sexual unfaithfulness as if it were **turning aside to uncleanness**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you did not do what is unclean and wrong]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **uncleanness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to do what is unclean]

Here, Yahweh could be using the phrase **under your husband** to indicate that: (1) the woman was married to her **husband** at the time. Alternate translation: [while married to your husband] (2) the uncleanness would have been committed with someone besides her **husband**. Alternate translation: [instead of your husband]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if this **water** were a captor from whom the woman could be **free**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [be unaffected by this water]

The priest is using the imperative form **be free** to state a promise rather than to give a command. He is telling the woman that if she has not committed adultery, she will not suffer any harm from drinking the water that brings a curse. If your language does not use an imperative form to express a promise, you could use a statement about the future. Alternate translation: [you will be free]
See how you translated this phrase in 5:18.

20.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking of unfaithfulness to one’s husband as if it were physically **turning aside** from the right path. See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:12. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you did what was wrong]
See how you translated this phrase in 5:19.

The expression **were made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you made yourself unclean]

Yahweh is referring to sexual relations in a polite way by using the phrase **gave his lying in you**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [a man had sexual relations with you] or [a man had intimate relations with you]

21.q: וְ⁠אָמַ֤ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵן֙ לָֽ⁠אִשָּׁ֔ה יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛⁠ךְ לְ⁠אָלָ֥ה וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑⁠ךְ בְּ⁠תֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְרֵכֵ⁠ךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְ⁠אֶת־בִּטְנֵ֖⁠ךְ צָבָֽה׃ וּ֠⁠בָאוּ הַ⁠מַּ֨יִם הַ⁠מְאָרְרִ֤ים הָ⁠אֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּֽ⁠מֵעַ֔יִ⁠ךְ לַ⁠צְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְ⁠לַ⁠נְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ
21.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And the priest shall tell the woman that Yahweh will give her to a curse and to an oath in the midst of her people when Yahweh gives her thigh falling and her belly swelling. He will tell her that this water that brings a curse will go in her insides to cause belly to swell and to cause thigh to fall.]

The implication is that the priest would speak the oath and then pause while the woman repeated the words after him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the priest shall stop speaking and shall make the woman swear]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an **oath** that contains **the curse**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the curse section of the oath]

21.q: יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛⁠ךְ לְ⁠אָלָ֥ה וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑⁠ךְ
21.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Yahweh were actually **giving** the woman to a **curse** and an **oath**. This means that Yahweh will bring about the consequences of the curse she speaks. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will make you suffer among your people what you swore in the curse and in the oath]

The phrase **curse and oath** expresses a single idea. The word **oath** tells more about **curse**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [to a curse in an oath]

21.q: בְּ⁠תֵ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְרֵכֵ⁠ךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְ⁠אֶת־בִּטְנֵ֖⁠ךְ צָבָֽה
21.note: Here the priest refers to general sickness or failure of female reproductive organs. These phrases are general and probably do not refer to one specific type of disease or failure. However, it is clear that the sickness or failure will prevent the conception and birth of children. Consider how to make this clear to your readers. Alternate translation: [when Yahweh gives your reproductive organs failure] or [when Yahweh makes you unable to bear children]

Yahweh is referring to sexual organs in a polite way by using the phrase **thigh**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [your genital organs]

22.note: See how you translated the similar phrases in 5:21.
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And the woman shall say amen twice.]

23.note: The implication is that **these curses** refers to the curse oath that the woman swore in 5:21. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the curses the woman spoke]

The priest is not referring to a specific **book**. He means a scroll or other writing material in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in a book]

The implication is that the priest will write the curses on a book or scroll and then wash off the ink into the water of bitterness so that the water contains the written curses. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and he shall use the water of bitterness to wash the words of the curses off the book into the water]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:18.

24.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:18.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **bitterness**, you could express the same idea in another way. This phrase is similar to the one earlier in the verse, so see how you translated the word **bitterness** there. Alternate translation: [the water that brings a curse and so makes bitter]

25.note: In 5:25–27, Yahweh explains the process by which the priest will have the woman drink the water, which is summarized in 5:24. If it would be helpful in your language, you could indicate that this is an explanation, not the next action in sequence. Alternate translation: [Specifically, the priest shall take] or [Before he has her drink the water, the priest shall take]
See how you translated this phrase in 5:15.

The **raising** of the grain offering was a symbolic action by which the priest showed that he was presenting the offering to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and he shall lift up the grain offering to the face of Yahweh to dedicate it to him]
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

Yahweh is using **present it to the altar** as a common expression of his culture to mean “bring it near to the altar.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall bring it near the altar]

26.note: The implication is the priest presented only a handful the grain offering to represent the entire offering before God and to serve as a memorial or reminder. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a handful, which is its memorial portion,]

27.note: It might seem that the expression **And he shall make her drink the water** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language since this was just stated in 5:26. If so, you can omit it.

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since **she was made unclean** describes the result and **was unfaithful in unfaithfulness against her husband** gives the reason for that result. Alternate translation: [she was unfaithful in unfaithfulness against her husband and so was made unclean]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 5:12.

The expression **was made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [she made herself unclean]
See how you translated this clause in 5:24.
See how you translated the similar phrases in 5:21.

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the woman herself were actually **a curse**. This refers to how she will experience the bad things in the **curse**, and **her people** will see this. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the woman will suffer among her people what she swore in the curse]

28.note: The phrases **the woman was not made unclean** and **she is clean** mean the same thing. For emphasis, Yahweh is saying it first negatively and then positively. If a speaker of your language would not use repetition like this, in your translation you can convey the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [the woman is completely clean]

The expression **was not made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the woman did not make herself unclean]

Here, the woman could be **free**: (1) from the negative affects of the water and the curse. This is what **free** explicitly refers to in 5:19. Alternate translation: [then she will be free of the water and the curse] (2) from any declaration of guilt. Alternate translation: [then she will be free of guilt]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and she will be sown successfully]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if a woman’s ability to have children were the same as if someone were planting **seed** in a field. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and she will be able to have children]

The expression **will be sown** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is her husband. Alternate translation: [and her husband will sow her with seed]

29.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **law** that is followed when there is **jealousy**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the law for dealing with jealousy]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **jealousy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the law for when a husband is jealous]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of a wife who is unfaithful to her husband as if she had physically **turned aside** from him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when a woman does what is wrong]
See how you translated this phrase in 5:19.

The expression **is made unclean** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and makes herself unclean]

30.q: תַּעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֛י⁠ו ר֥וּחַ קִנְאָ֖ה וְ⁠קִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֑⁠וֹ
30.note: See how you translated the same sentence in 5:14.
Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

Here, **all this law** represents the specific instructions given for the test of jealousy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everything that this law states]

31.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the ideas of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from doing wrong … what she did wrong]
Here, the word **iniquity** could refer to: (1) punishment because of **iniquity**. Alternate translation: [from punishment] (2) guilt because of **iniquity**. Alternate translation: [from guilt]

By **this woman**, Yahweh means the woman who has committed adultery. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the woman who is guilty]

Here, Yahweh speaks of being punished for **iniquity** as if it were lifting up that **iniquity**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will bear her iniquity] or [will be punished for her iniquity]
